Confidential working guide01 / 09
01 / Brand foundation

What the brand must feel like

Vision should feel like a club that is progressing — not merely participating. The visual system combines the authority of deep violet with the energy of magenta and the optimism of gold.

Brand character

AmbitiousExpressiveDisciplinedProudForward-looking

Young in energy, serious in standards. Competitive without becoming hostile; local in pride, modern in presentation.

Core promise

Vision gives talented people a platform to see further, work harder and play with purpose.

This is the strategic idea behind the website, match-day graphics, recruitment materials and social content.

Messaging pillars

01 / See further

Progress, possibility and intelligent football.

02 / Earn the badge

Work ethic, character and accountability.

03 / Represent with pride

Club, community, Ghana and the next generation.

02 / Colour system

Energy with authority

Use violet as the anchor, magenta as the signal and gold as the moment of emphasis. White space is not optional: it gives the crest and the message room to breathe.

Vision Violet#3D0B63

Primary field, headers, digital backgrounds and formal applications.

Signal Magenta#C415B4

Calls to action, highlights, motion accents and selected text.

Stadium Purple#6220A3

Secondary surfaces, gradients and supporting graphics.

Matchday Gold#F1CF20

Scores, wins, badges, trim and moments that need attention.

Supporting neutrals

Kit White#FFFFFF
Soft Mist#F6F3F8
Ink#171020
Colour ratio

60% white/mist  ·  25% violet/purple  ·  10% magenta  ·  5% gold

The values are working approximations sampled from the supplied low-resolution crest. Confirm against the original vector artwork before producing kits or print at scale.

03 / Typography

A sharper voice

The logo uses a condensed, arched display style. The recommended digital pairing keeps that sporting character while remaining highly legible on mobile.

Display / Barlow Condensed

See the
game differently

Weights: SemiBold, Bold, ExtraBold

Use for headlines, fixtures, scorelines, player names, short statements and navigation labels. Uppercase is preferred for high-impact moments; use sentence case for longer headlines.

Body / Manrope

Built for clarity.
Vision Football Club is a modern Ghanaian football institution with a clear eye on the future.

Weights: Regular, Medium, SemiBold, Bold

Use for paragraphs, captions, metadata, forms and longer digital content. Keep line length comfortable and avoid all-caps body copy.

Type rules

  • Headlines should be short, active and confident: “The future plays here.”
  • Use a maximum of two typefaces in any composition.
  • Keep display tracking slightly open in all-caps to echo the crest lettering.
  • Never stretch, skew or artificially condense the body font.
  • Use gold sparingly for emphasis, not as a long paragraph colour.

Typography04 / 09
04 / Crest and logo use

Protect the badge

The crest is the club’s highest-value asset. It should remain recognisable at a glance and should never be treated as a decorative sticker.

Clear space

crest

Maintain clear space equal to the height of the “V” in VISION on all sides. Increase the space where possible.

Preferred applications

  • Full-colour crest on white or very pale mist.
  • Reversed crest on Vision Violet when the white details remain visible.
  • Single-colour white mark only when production demands it.
  • Use the full crest for formal club communications; use the wordmark or monogram for compact digital placements.

Do / don’t

DO
Keep the crest upright, proportional, crisp and surrounded by space. Use high-resolution master artwork.
DON’T
Recolour individual crest parts, add shadows, rotate it, crop the text, or place it on a visually noisy photograph.
DO
Use the gold ring as a premium accent and preserve the visual hierarchy of the original badge.
DON’T
Recreate the badge from the screenshot for production. Request or redraw a clean vector master first.
Production note: The supplied reference is 340 × 567 px and includes surrounding page content. It is suitable for direction-setting only, not for print, kit embroidery or final web export.
Crest governance05 / 09
05 / Photography and art direction

Real ambition, vividly told

Photography should feel close, energetic and earned. Avoid generic football stock imagery. The club’s advantage is its real people, real ground and real journey.

Photography

  • Low, purposeful camera angles that make players feel ready, not untouchable.
  • Warm Ghanaian daylight, late-afternoon gold and honest stadium texture.
  • Faces, hands, boots, kit detail, preparation and community — not only action shots.
  • Use magenta/violet colour grading lightly; skin tones must remain natural.

Suggested art style

MATCHDAY
Make
your mark.
◉

Graphic language: bold condensed type, diagonal motion lines, crest geometry, cropped circles, star points and controlled halftone texture.

Illustration and motion

Geometry

Use arcs, rings and diagonal cuts derived from the crest — never random decoration.

Texture

Use restrained grain, halftone and paper/paint texture to add physicality.

Movement

Animate sweeps, rings and type reveals from left to right: always forward.

AI image guidance: If AI-generated imagery is commissioned later, it should be used for atmospheric campaign concepts or abstract backgrounds, not as a substitute for authentic player, supporter or match photography. Any production image work should use the approved GPT Image 2 workflow and be reviewed for kit, crest and likeness accuracy.
Art direction06 / 09
06 / Digital expression

Built for the phone first

The club’s audience will often meet the brand on Instagram, Facebook, WhatsApp and a mobile browser. The identity must therefore work at speed and at small sizes.

Website direction

  • Hero: one strong image, one clear statement, one action.
  • Primary actions: Latest result, Next fixture, Join the journey.
  • Use violet navigation and white content zones for trust and readability.
  • Reserve magenta for active states; gold for match importance and success.

Social system

  • Matchday: violet base + gold date/time + magenta opponent cue.
  • Result: large condensed scoreline, minimal copy.
  • Player: portrait crop, name, position, short human detail.
  • Community: warmer photography, mist background, violet type.

Do’s and don’ts

DO
Lead with the information supporters need: opponent, time, venue, score, ticket or contact path.
DON’T
Make supporters hunt through a cinematic homepage to find the next match.
DO
Write like a confident club representative: warm, direct and proud.
DON’T
Overuse slogans, exclamation marks or vague “we are the best” claims.
Digital system07 / 09
07 / Voice and language

Confident, never inflated

Voice principles

  • Clear: say what happened and what happens next.
  • Ambitious: talk about progress with evidence and intent.
  • Human: recognise players, staff, supporters and community.
  • Composed: let performance create the drama.

Message examples

Fixture:
“The next test is set. Vision FC welcome [opponent] to Tema.”

Result:
“Three points. One team. We move forward.”

Community:
“The badge belongs to everyone who carries Vision forward.”

Words to favour

ForwardPurposeEarnedTogetherProgressPrideNext

Words to avoid

UnstoppableWorld-classDominantBest ever

Avoid claims that cannot be substantiated. The club should sound hungry, not boastful.

Recommended working tagline

See the game
differently.

Use as an institutional line while campaign lines can change by season or objective.

08 / Implementation checklist

Make it real

This guide is a strategic first edition. Before the website goes live, the following assets should be formalised and approved.

Priority assets

  1. Clean vector crest: AI, SVG and PDF.
  2. Approved wordmark and compact VFC monogram.
  3. Official colour values confirmed in CMYK, RGB and HEX.
  4. Font licensing and webfont files.
  5. Player, team, ground and community photography.
  6. Fixture/result data source and contact details.

Website launch test

  • Can a supporter find the next fixture in under 5 seconds?
  • Does the crest remain legible at mobile header size?
  • Are all football facts current and sourced?
  • Is there a direct WhatsApp/contact route?
  • Do colours meet accessible contrast standards?
  • Does the site feel like Vision — not a generic template?

Recommended next step

Secure the original crest file and approve this visual direction before designing the website interface. That single decision prevents the site from being built around a low-resolution screenshot and gives every future asset a stable foundation.
